inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to conclude renegotiation of the 2009 agreement, threatening an indefinite nationwide strike if its demands are not met. Government should honour its obligations, but holding universities hostage is no way to resolve a dispute: students and families should not be made to bear the cost of a breakdown in negotiations. Both sides need to act responsibly and reach a settlement before another strike disrupts university life.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to renegotiate the 2009 agreement or face an indefinite nationwide strike. The government should honour its obligations, but no union has the right to make students and families pay for a dispute between adults. Universities exist to educate, not to serve as leverage in a standoff. Both sides must put duty and the future of young people ahead of brinkmanship and settle this before university life is disrupted again.
